Synopsis:
Arron is a friendly, but tired servant to the druids in the grove. Unless the player is a druid, he would rather they don't linger, though he is sympathetic and will help them any way he can (by selling them supplies). He is happy to see a druid and to help them. He can be a little preachy.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_DruidServant_005.json: Arron is a tired but well‑meaning servant of the Emerald Grove who prefers druids and would rather outsiders not linger — he’s sympathetic, a little preachy, and runs a modest supply table for anyone who needs gear. The grove is preparing a drastic ritual that will shroud it in thorny vines and lock it down — Arron warns that in a few days no one will be able to enter or leave and urges visitors to act quickly. Off‑screen there’ve been recent goblin skirmishes around the wolf pens (and the party may have driven off or fought those goblins and their beast), so he thanks the player for help and points wounded seekers to Nettie in the inner chambers while noting supplies are limited. If the player is a druid Arron is noticeably more welcoming; otherwise he’s polite but insistent the grove’s survival comes first.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_Servant005.json: Arron, a druid trader, is truly relieved that the player was able to help everyone. He didn't look forward to what would have happened otherwise.
- DEN_DruidServant_002.json: Marcoryl is a condescending druid servant at the Emerald Grove who openly distrusts and despises the tiefling refugees, preferring to turn them away even if that dooms them. The player has apparently convinced Kagha to shelter or spare the tieflings, and Marcoryl’s line (“You may have won over Kagha…”) calls out his refusal to be persuaded. Off‑screen violence tied to the nearby goblin camp — recent attacks and the death of a child — has inflamed his anger; he blames opening the grove’s gates for the chaos. His remark about the “smell of sulphur” signals visceral prejudice against the tieflings’ fiendish nature and explains his hostility.
- DEN_SacredPond_RitualDruid1.json: This dialogue can occur in three different states: In the first, Aelar is in a trance, chanting a spell that will cover the druid grove in thorns. In the second, the ritual has been stopped after a druid named Kagha was exposed as a Shadow Druid. Aelar is in a daze - several days of chanting have left him a bit loopy.In the third, a group of goblins that had threatened the grove has been dealt with and the grove is considered safe again. In this state, Aelar is still exhausted, but he's gathered his senses, more or less. The player always encounters Aelar around a sacred druid pool.
- DEN_SacredPond_RitualDruid2.json: This dialogue can occur in three different states: In the first, Kerrick is in a trance, chanting a spell that will cover the druid grove in thorns. In the second, the ritual has been stopped after a druid named Kagha was exposed as a Shadow Druid. Kerrick is furious - he feels betrayed by Kagha, and doesn't quite care if she's been killed.In the third, a group of goblins that had threatened the grove has been dealt with and the grove is considered safe again. In this state, Kerrick has calmed down a good bit - now that the danger's passed, he's seeing things with a bit more clarity. The player always encounters Kerrick around a sacred druid pool.

context: Arron is a tired but well‑meaning servant who runs a modest supply table for the Emerald Grove and prefers druids — he’s polite to outsiders but would rather they not linger. Off‑screen there have been recent goblin skirmishes (around the wolf pens), and Arron is relieved if the player helped drive them off; he thanks the player and points wounded seekers to Nettie in the inner chambers. The grove is preparing a drastic ritual that, in a few days, will shroud the place in thorny vines and prevent anyone entering or leaving, so supplies and medical care are limited and Arron urges visitors to act quickly. He’s sympathetic and a bit preachy about the grove’s survival coming first, but will help (and sell gear) to those in need — and is noticeably more welcoming if the visitor is a druid.
